name: Rings and Algebras

papers.title: Nonzero central quotients of the Virasoro enveloping algebra are simple
papers.abstract: We prove a conjecture of Petukhov and Sierra that the central quotient $\mathrm{U}(\mathrm{Vir})/(z-c)$ of the universal enveloping algebra of the Virasoro algebra is simple for all $c \neq 0$. We extend the result to the $N=1$ super-Virasoro algebras. Our proof reveals a new connection between enveloping algebras and polynomial identity algebras. Although the enveloping algebra itself does not satisfy a polynomial identity, the adjoint action on each filtered piece does satisfy a standard identity. In particular, the Witt algebra $W$, as an adjoint module over itself, satisfies the standard identity $\mathrm{St}_4$, whereas $\mathrm{Vir}$ fails by a nonzero multiple of the central charge. Propagating this gap through the PBW filtration of $\mathrm{U}(\mathrm{Vir})/(z-c)$, for every nonscalar element, we construct an alternating adjoint operator that lowers its order by exactly one. As applications, we compute the annihilators of all representations with nonzero central character, prove a strengthened form of Etingof's conjecture on nonsplit extensions of $W$-modules, and reduce the classification of prime ideals of $\mathrm{U}(\mathrm{Vir})$ to those of $\mathrm{U}(W)$.

papers.title: Parallel sums of nilpotent elements: exact realization and structured eigenvalue splitting
papers.abstract: We prove that, over every infinite field and for $m\ge2$, the parallel sums $N(N+C)^{-1}C$ of nilpotent $m\times m$ inputs with invertible sum are exactly the matrices of nullity at least two. Every positive split of the target nullity between the input kernels is realizable. Over $\mathbb{C}$, we determine the paired derivative image and characterize universal full matrix cancellation at nonzero residues. For analytic input paths, nilpotence is required only at the base. An adjugate identity forces the last two characteristic coefficients to be $O(\varepsilon^2)$, yielding sharp bounds $O(|\varepsilon|^{2/3})$ at nonzero three-dimensional nilpotent residues and $O(|\varepsilon|^{1/(m-2)})$ at nilpotent residues for $m\ge4$. At every base with residue of type $[m-1,1]$, $m\ge4$, we prove a generic splitting law, also with fixed input sum. For $m\ge5$, it has $m-2$ roots on the scale $|\varepsilon|^{1/(m-2)}$ and two on the scale $|\varepsilon|^{1/2}$, separating the largest-root and spectral-gap scales. A separate sharpness family keeps both inputs nilpotent and two roots zero. At the nonzero nilpotent three-dimensional boundary, a finite coefficient criterion computes the splitting orders for each exceptional affine fixed-sum direction. For each such path, the punctured spectral gap is at least $c|\varepsilon|^3$ near zero for some $c>0$, and the exponent is optimal over this class. Over a nonzero unital ring with $2$ invertible, we construct two $3\times3$ matrix inputs, each of nilpotency index exactly three, with invertible sum. In the complex unital Banach case, the residue has spectrum ${0}\cup\tfrac12\sigma(Q)$ for every coefficient $Q$. With the common core allowed to vary, a complex matrix is a finite-Drazin Hua output if and only if its nullity is not one.

papers.title: A Sweedler dual seen as a terminal object in a category of bialgebras
papers.abstract: We study the Sweedler dual of the polynomial algebra $\mathbb{K}[X]$ equipped with the multiplicative coproduct $\delta(X) = X \otimes X$, and show that the resulting bialgebra $\mathbb{K}[X]^\star$ is the terminal object in the category of pairs $(B, \lambda)$, where $B$ is a bialgebra and $\lambda$ is a character of $B$. This generalizes a result of Aguiar, Bergeron, and Sottile on combinatorial Hopf algebras in the graded and connected setting. We describe the subcoalgebras and subbialgebras of $\mathbb{K}[X]^\star$, which lead to the introduction of the spectrum of a bialgebra. We also study the particular cases double bialgebras (bialgebras equipped with two compatible coproducts), firstly examining their connection to unital near-semirings or near-rings. Introducing a subbialgebra of $\mathbb{K}[X]^\star$ obtained from the intersection with another Sweedler dual, we prove it is the terminal object in the category of double bialgebras. As a consequence, we show that the spectrum of any double Hopf algebra is a subgroup of the group of roots of unity. This imply that not any bialgebra can become double. We finally apply this framework to a bialgebra of graphs with a coproduct given by contraction and deletion of edges, relating its invariants to Bergman colorations of edges arising from graphical matroids.

papers.title: A square analogue of the diamond order and a unified approach to the plus order
papers.abstract: We introduce the square order $\le^\square$ on group invertible matrices, defined by $A^3=ABA$ and $A\le^s B$, where $\le^s$ is the space pre-order. It is the group inverse analogue of the diamond order: $A\le^\square B$ if and only if $A^\#\le^- B^\#$. Using its block representation, we characterize the reverse order law $(AB)^\#=B^\#A^\#$ for $A\le^\square B$. In contrast to the Moore--Penrose case, the conditions $A\le^- B$ and $(B-A)^\#=B^\#-A^\#$ do not characterize the sharp order; instead, they lead to new partial orders between the sharp and square orders. We also develop a framework where the plus order replaces the minus order in Mitra's unified theory. For a map $\mathcal G$ assigning to each matrix $A$ a subset of its inner inverses, we define $A\le^{\mathcal G}_{+}B$ if $A\le^s B$ and $A=PBQ$ for some pair $(P,Q)=(AA^-,A^-A)$, $A^-\in\mathcal G(A)$, whereas Mitra's relation requires $A=PB=BQ$, and $A\preceq^{\mathcal G}_{+}B$ if $A\le^s B$ and $A^-\le^-B^-$ for some reflexive $A^-\in\mathcal G(A)$ and $B^-\in\mathcal G(B)$. When $\mathcal G(A)$ consists of a single reflexive inverse, we characterize the transitivity of $\le^{\mathcal G}_{+}$ in terms of $\preceq^{\mathcal G}_{+}$, and in general we give a sufficient condition for both to be partial orders. For maps defined by the equations of the Moore--Penrose, group, core and dual core inverses, both relations coincide and only nine arise: the plus, diamond and square orders, two new orders based on core inverses, and four further relations. In Mitra's theory, they yield exactly the minus, star, sharp, core and dual core orders and the one-sided star and sharp orders.

papers.title: Separation formulas for non-normalized generalized cluster algebras
papers.abstract: We study a class of not necessarily normalized generalized cluster patterns which are uniquely determined by the initial seed and mutations. For such generalized cluster patterns, we provide the separation formulas for cluster variables and coefficients.

papers.title: Polynomial identities and primitivity in double extension regular algebras of type (14641)
papers.abstract: We determine which members of the twenty-six families of double extension regular algebras of type $(14641)$ in the Zhang--Zhang classification satisfy a polynomial identity. Retaining the scalar twist parameter, we compute the PI degree for twenty-one of the twenty-two families with PI members and give three possibilities for the remaining family. We establish exact primitivity criteria for the nondegenerate members of eight families and show that sixteen families have no primitive members. The proofs use monomial data, normal subalgebras and crossed products of quantum tori. Twisting by a root of unity preserves the PI property, whereas finite order of the double-extension determinant is necessary but not sufficient for an algebra in the list to be PI.

papers.title: Galois scalar extension of simple Lie algebras
papers.abstract: We investigate the behaviour of simple finite-dimensional Lie algebras under finite Galois field extensions. Given a simple Lie algebra $L$ over a field $\mathbb{F}$ and a finite Galois extension $\mathbb{K}/\mathbb{F}$ of degree $n = [\mathbb{K}:\mathbb{F}]$, we prove that if $L$ is isomorphic to a $\mathbb{K}$-Lie algebra $S$ viewed as an $\mathbb{F}$-algebra, then the scalar extension $L \otimes_{\mathbb{F}} \mathbb{K}$ is isomorphic to the direct sum of $n$ copies of $S$. Furthermore, for cyclic extensions of order a prime number, we show that if no such $\mathbb{K}$-Lie algebra $S$ exists, the extended algebra $L \otimes_{\mathbb{F}} \mathbb{K}$ remains simple. This framework provides a general mechanism to transfer structural and classification results across different ground fields. In addition, we examine the centroids of simple Lie algebras, proving that the dimension of the space of centroids is invariant under finite field extensions. As an application, we explicitly determine the structure of the spaces of centroids for simple Lie algebras over finite fields.

papers.title: Stability in abstract classes via set theoretic techniques
papers.abstract: We prove that all abstract classes equipped with an independence relation satisfying a mild local character condition are stable. We obtain the result by using methods from model theory and set theory. We have several applications in the context of abstract classes of modules. In particular, we prove that if $K$ is a class of $R$-modules closed under isomorphisms and pure submodules and $\lambda^{\operatorname{card}(R) + \aleph_0} = \lambda$, then $K$ equipped with pure embeddings is stable in $\lambda$.

papers.title: On Zappa--Szép products of multiplicative racks
papers.abstract: We study Zappa--Sz\'ep products of multiplicative racks, namely monoids equipped with compatible rack operations. We characterize multiplicative rack structures on Zappa--Sz\'ep products of monoids and prove that every exact factorization of multiplicative racks induces a canonical exact factorization of their universal groups. We also establish exact factorizations of groups of units and cancellative quotients, show that reduction modulo units yields a direct product, and obtain consequences for Ore localization. We then generalize Bianchi's construction using augmentations from partially multiplicative racks into arbitrary multiplicative racks and establish a reconstruction theorem for multiplicative racks with suitable unital ideals. We investigate the interaction between unital ideals and exact factorizations, and characterize Zappa--Sz\'ep factorizations of generalized Bianchi-type multiplicative racks. Finally, we use a layered central-quotient construction to obtain finite and infinite non-cancellative multiplicative quandles with non-group factors and nontrivial Zappa--Sz\'ep actions, all directly indecomposable as monoids.
